C^1 with J(delta - d0 f), inf over f in C^0

relations.statement: inf_f J(delta + d0 g - d0 f) = inf_h J(delta - d0 h) via h = f - g, a bijection of C^0
relations.hypotheses: none; d0 linear, f -> f - g bijective

relations.statement: inf is attained after quotienting ker d0
relations.hypotheses: repair space finite-dimensional over R or C and J a norm (not seminorm)
positive weights w, finite-dimensional weighted graph complex, imported strong duality REF-MATH-005 (assumption)

lemmas.statement: For all delta, g in C^0, inf_f J(delta + d0 g - d0 f) = inf_f J(delta - d0 f).
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem rep_indep {V W : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [AddCommGroup W] (d : V →+ W) (J : W → ℝ) (δ : W) (g : V) : sInf (Set.range fun f => J (δ + d g - d f)) = sInf (Set.range fun f => J (δ - d f)) := by sorry

lemmas.statement: Weak duality: for y with d0*y=0 and |y_e|<=w_e, <y,delta> <= weighted l1 J(delta - d0 f) for every f.

near_misses.claim: Attainment holds for a seminorm J
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Seminorm has nontrivial kernel; the infimum over unbounded directions need not be attained, so the norm hypothesis is needed.
Compactness of sublevel sets of the quotient fails without finite dimension.
